entry.name: M2VTP BottleCap
entry.title: Masked Visual-Tactile Pre-training for Robot Manipulation
entry.summary: Human bottle-cap turning recorded with a low-cost Zhejiang University glove giving 20 binary touch signals and egocentric HoloLens 2 video, released as per-sequence PNG frame folders with one tactile pickle per sequence; sequence count not published in the sources read.
entry.hand: Custom low-cost tactile glove (Zhejiang University), 20 sensors

sensor.note: Abstract and project page: '20 sparse binary tactile signals sensing touch states'. The pretraining code loads tactile/<vid>.pkl per sequence and marks a frame as touching when any value reaches a threshold argument, so the files may hold raw values before binarisation. Sensor placement, principle and rate not read; files not opened.

scale.text: one task (bottle-cap turning); sequence, frame, object and subject counts not published in the sources read

entry.access: One OneDrive file linked from the Pretraining_for_M2VTP README ('Please download the dataset from the following link'), no password or form mentioned; it unpacks to data/raw/BottleCap with labels/, tactile/ and videos/. Size not visible to a script; download not tested.
caveats: Files not opened: the OneDrive share page returns no file listing to a script, so size, sequence count and tactile value range are unknown.
Touch is 20 discrete signals that the paper treats as binary touch states, not a pressure map.
Video is per-frame PNG folders (videos/<vid>/*.png, ordered by the number after the last '='), as read by the authors' preprocessing code; no timestamps were seen.
One task only (bottle-cap turning); the later VTDexManip release from the same group covers 10 tasks with a 20-pad glove, and whether it contains these sequences was not checked.
The paper is not open access; IEEE Xplore returned an empty page and ResearchGate returned 403, so the entry rests on the abstract, the project page and the two READMEs.
